title: Why was Davy Crockett king of the wild frontier?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explore the life of Davy Crockett, the Tennessee frontiersman, militia fighter, Congressman, and Alamo defender who became a national legend. They cover his childhood and escape from a cattle-driving job, his militia service in the Creek War and Indian removal, his opposition to Andrew Jackson's Indian Removal Act that cost him his congressional seat, his "go to Texas" remark, his death at the Siege of the Alamo, and how Disney's 1950s Davy Crockett TV series and coonskin cap craze revived his legend. The episode ends with a listener email about civil rights for psychiatric patients and a sponsor read.

segments.title: Opening banter and Davy Crockett nostalgia
segments.summary: Hosts welcome Jerry back from back surgery, then reminisce about childhood Davy Crockett costumes and the Disney TV show, and introduce the topic.

segments.title: Davy Crockett's legend and Disney fever
segments.summary: Discussion of Crockett as the symbol of westward expansion, his Tennessee roots, the 1950s Disney series and coonskin cap sales, the 'King of the Wild Frontier' theme song, and the legends that blur fact and fiction.

segments.title: Army Davy Crockett nuclear rocket
segments.summary: A digression on the 1960s U.S. Army Davy Crockett weapon, a lightweight launcher that fired nuclear-warhead mortars; it was tested but never used in battle.

segments.title: Childhood, escape from Silas, and leaving school
segments.summary: Crockett at age twelve is sent to drive cattle, is held as a virtual slave by Jacob Siler, escapes by a seven-mile night hike in snow, then skips school and leaves home at about sixteen before returning and working off his father's debt.

segments.title: Militia service and Indian removal
segments.summary: Crockett joins Tennessee militias and fights in the campaign against Southern Indian nations, including the Tallushatchee attack in Alabama alongside Andrew Jackson. The hosts describe the treaties that forced removal and Crockett's early political posts as town commissioner and justice of the peace.

segments.title: Congress, opposition to Jackson, and defeat
segments.summary: Crockett is elected to the Tennessee legislature and then to Congress, where he opposes Jackson's Indian Removal Act and the Supreme Court's discovery-based ruling. He loses his third bid narrowly. He later helps subdue a would-be assassin of Jackson on the Capitol steps. He turns to making barrel staves, and the hosts recount tall tales and the Crockett Almanacs and autobiography.

segments.title: Texas, the Alamo, and his death
segments.summary: After losing to Adam Huntsman, Crockett says he will go to Texas, joins the Texas rebellion, signs its oath, and dies at the Siege of the Alamo. Accounts differ, and a Mexican soldier's diary later indicated that Crockett was captured and executed with a handful of others.

segments.title: Legacy and closing thoughts on national heroes
segments.summary: Hosts reflect on how Crockett's death cemented his legend and wonder what equivalent national heroes exist in other countries, and invite listeners to share them.

segments.title: Listener mail: consumer survivor movement
segments.summary: Listener Jamie asks the show to cover the consumer survivor movement and psychiatric patient civil rights, citing ECT, forced medication, and anti-psychiatry activism.

segments.title: Outro and sponsor
segments.summary: Hosts sign off with listener contact information and a State Farm sponsor line.
